newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-MONTY IN DANGER OF MISSING OPEN CUT AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTY IN DANGER OF MISSING OPEN CUT AGAIN.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie, so close to victory at last month's U.S. Open, fell victim to his home-town course at the British Open golf championship on Thursday.
On the Royal Troon links where he learned the game as a boy and where his father James has been secretary for 11 years, Monty went through a nightmare as he soared to a five-over par 76.
That left him facing a possible fifth missed halfway cut in six years at the Open, though he said defiantly he would play better on Friday and could break par.
The Scot denied that nerves or the fearsome wind that blew into the golfers' faces on the back nine had anything to do with his disaster.
He said it was caused by pushing balls to the right all day as, after the third hole, he failed to hit a single fairway.
That was a painful admission for a player who is proud of his usual ability to drive the ball straight.
"I just kept pushing most of the shots. Possibly I just was not coming through the ball and I'll try this afternoon to find out the problem," he said.
"I was aggressive and felt good but unfortunately I didn't play very well today.
"It wasn't nerves because I was two under-par after six holes and that would have been where I would be nervous.
"And the back nine is perfectly playable even in this wind if you hit the fairways. I can birdie any hole out there and I am confident of doing that," he said.
He did not offer any excuse for his poor driving, saying: "I should be able to hit more fairways that that, knowing the wind and the strength of it and where to hit the ball on the course.
"I knew the lines, obviously, but I couldn't hit the ball on those particular lines today."

Montgomerie has been second in three majors, losing a playoff to Ernie Els in the 1994 U.S. Open and losing to Els by one shot again at that event last month. He lost the 1995 U.S. PGA Championship to Australian Steve Elkington in a playoff and is still searching for his first major.

He was considered one of the favourites here after his U.S. Open showing and his victory since then in the Irish Open, where he fired a Druids Glen course record 62 in the final round to win by seven shots.
"It's disappointing when you shoot 76 in a major championship, and especially as a Briton in the British Open.
"Whether or not I do well tomorrow, I'll come back from this and it won't hurt. But it's just such a shame that it had to happen at home."
